To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have created a set of tools that allow us to perform a dynamic analysis of android applications, in order to find malicious code and to generate the necessary inputs that trigger the malicious code, in order to be able to perform the analysis.

We have successfully developed and integrated two software tools, namely JITANA and APTES to automatically generate a set of input events to trigger potential malicious behaviors in mobile applications, which can be used in the dynamic analysis phase of the mobile application security testing.

1) The proposed approach of using dynamic analysis for Android malware detection has been successfully implemented and tested on 2000+ apps, 2) The developed tool JITANA can generate a large number of inputs for Android Apps in a very short time and can be used for testing Android apps for maliciousness, 3) The developed tool APEX can be used to generate inputs for Android Apps and can be used to test the maliciousness of the Android Apps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing tools to automatically test Android Apps for malware.
developing a set of software tools for the dynamic analysis of Android apps.
developing a dynamic analysis tool that is capable of automatically vetting for malware features in Android platforms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a framework for automatic vetting for malice in Android platforms.
, the proposed tools are effective in generating inputs to trigger malicious features of Android apps.
, the tools developed in this project are capable to generate a set of events (inputs) for the dynamic analysis of mobile apps in order to expose malicious features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed two tools that can be used in conjunction with each other to perform dynamic analysis for Android Apps.
we have successfully implemented a dynamic analysis framework for Android applications.
we have developed a set of tools to help in Android App Security Testing by providing the inputs needed to trigger malicious features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to automatically generate a set of inputs that can be used for dynamic analysis of mobile apps.
the tools we developed can be used for dynamic analysis of Android applications.
we can generate a sequence of inputs that are capable of revealing a set of malicious targets.
